thread:
maria: Heads up - nightly SAST/DAST run flagged a high-sev potential dependency injection in auth-proxy. stack-trace attached by scan-bot below. Can someone triage?
scan-bot: [auto] SAST found: `AuthProxy::parse_user_input` -> unsanitized template usage. Severity: HIGH. CI run id: ci/2026-03-21/nightly-4412.
kevin: I see that. Repro locally with the same binary?
jonathan: Not yet. Also noticed that the artifact audit logs are blank for the scan window (00:00-02:00 UTC). Looks like KMS access for the scanner service account failed during artifact fetch.
maria: Oh that's bad. If the scanner couldn't decrypt artifacts, the finding could be a false-positive or missing context. @kevin any recent RBAC changes to scanner SA?
kevin: We rotated a key last week and tightened the bucket policy for a short window while rolling. I thought we added the scanner SA to the new binding. I’ll check iam binding now.
kevin: quick output: `gsutil iam get gs://redwood-ci-artifacts | grep scanner-service-account` -> returns nothing. Ugh.
maria: That would explain empty audit entries and partial artifacts. We need: 1) restore scanner SA access to decrypt artifacts; 2) backfill artifact access audit logs if possible; 3) triage SAST finding after verifying full artifact.
jonathan: For immediate restoration, we can grant temporary role storage.objectViewer + storage.objects.get and a KMS decrypt binding for the scanner SA. I'll prepare a temp grant and log it in the audit channel.
oncall-bot: Incident created: #sec-incident-2026-03-21-4412. Pager duty notified. Include runbook step id: sdlc-009.
maria: Good. Kevin, please do the temp grant with a TTL of 2 hours and paste the grant command here. Also include KMS key name.
kevin: Running: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-ci --member=serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/storage.objectViewer`
kevin: And KMS grant: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/artifact-decrypt --member=serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`
maria: Paste the auditlog link once available. Also, can we backfill logs? jonathan?
jonathan: We can pull object access logs from the storage logging bucket if retention exists. If not, GCS will have logs in the log sink for past 7 days. I'll query: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="gcs_bucket" AND protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp' --limit 1000 --start="2026-03-21T00:00:00Z" --end="2026-03-21T02:00:00Z"`
jonathan: Early result: KMS decrypt requests returned 403 for scanner SA at 00:12 UTC. That matches rotation window.
maria: OK that confirms. Action plan: 1) Temp grant (kevin) 2) Re-run the SAST/DAST job (scan-bot) 3) If finding persists on full artifact, open vuln-ticket with label `sdlc:triage` and assign to kevin. 4) Update runbook for key rotations to include scanner SA preflight.
kevin: Temp grants applied. I'll kick off the re-run now.
scan-bot: [auto] Re-run queued: ci/2026-03-21/nightly-4412-rerun. Estimated finish ~10m.
maria: Also we should add a guard in the rotation playbook: automation test that attempts a dry-decrypt with scanner SA post-rotation and fails the rotation if decrypt fails. That would prevent this gap.
jonathan: Agreed. I'll add a test step to the rotation pipeline and a short audit webhook that posts status to #eng-security.
kevin: Re-run finished. New scan output: low-confidence/not-repro for the DI pattern after artifact full-read. Looks like the original finding was from a truncated file.
maria: Marking the finding as NOT_EXPLOITABLE for now but opening a follow-up ticket to harden parsing in AuthProxy and add unit tests. Also record the RBAC gap and key-rotation preflight change in the runbook.
maria: Follow-up tasks: `/todo` - (1) ticket sdlc-311: patch auth-proxy parsing (assigned kevin), (2) rotation-pipeline PR (assigned jonathan), (3) audit log retention check (assigned maria).
jonathan: I'll set retention to 90 days for storage logs and add a separate sink for KMS audit events.
kevin: Thanks. Learned that tighten-first, verify-second is dangerous for infra that supports automated scanners.
maria: Agreed. Closing incident once docs/PRs are merged. :thumbsup:
